recentItems.title: US Troop Surge Changes Mexico Border Scene As Army Shows Once-Busy River Crossing | Watch
recentItems.description:
The US Army is deploying hundreds of additional troops to Texas’ Rio Grande Valley as the Trump administration expands border security operations against illegal crossings, drug trafficking and cartel activity. The military says its efforts, supported by the Coast Guard and increased cooperation with Mexico, have helped disrupt smuggling networks. Mexico has also deployed 500 National Guard and military personnel to Tamaulipas for coordinated operations. However, experts question the need for such a large military presence, arguing that most seized drugs enter through official ports of entry and that falling crossings largely reflect asylum restrictions. The debate continues over the effectiveness of the deployment and whether it delivers lasting security benefits or serves a political purpose.

recentItems.title: Marco Rubio To Visit India: Oil & Energy Cooperation On Agenda | US-India Trade Deal To Reset?
recentItems.description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to visit India, with oil and energy cooperation expected to feature prominently on the agenda. The visit comes amid ongoing efforts to strengthen US-India ties and revive trade negotiations. He is also set to visit Jamnagar during his India his India visit. Could Rubio’s trip pave the way for a breakthrough in the US-India trade deal?

recentItems.title: Bolsonaro Faces Backlash! President Lula Camp Hits Streets In Brazil Ahead Of Second Round
recentItems.description:
Supporters of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gathered at São Paulo’s Largo da Batata amid rain to demonstrate their backing ahead of the October 25 presidential run-off. Lula faces Senator Flávio Bolsonaro after the first round on October 4, in which Bolsonaro received 47.03% of the vote and Lula secured 45.16%, according to the supplied report. The rally featured political figures including Fernando Haddad, Simone Tebet and Marina Silva. Demonstrators voiced concerns over workers’ rights, women’s rights and national sovereignty, while calling for greater political mobilisation ahead of the decisive vote.
